mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as low interest rates reduce discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as rising joblessness signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% over the past month predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as a supply shock coupled with labor market deterioration signals a deepening economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when INDPRO falls > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.2% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles defined by FEDFUNDS exceeding 1.0% and annualized CPIAUCSL growth exceeding 2.5%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days are negative, as higher interest rates and inflationary pressures reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in less than 40% of instances during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS>1.0% and CPIAUCSL annualized>2.5%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 600 consistently predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as strong residential construction activity signals robust economic growth and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when HOUST > 600, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level below 550 predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as declining residential construction signals economic contraction and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 40% of instances when HOUST < 550, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% over the past month predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as a dual weakness in residential construction and investment signals a broad-based economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 0.5% and RSAFS falls > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when HOUST falls > 0.5% and RSAFS falls > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening regime defined by monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% and unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days are positive, as strong labor market conditions support consumer spending and corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in less than 40% of instances during labor market tightening regimes (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE < 5.0%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
